# Line spacing not working correctly for AT_LEAST rule in paragraph formatting

## Description

I'm having an issue with setting line spacing in paragraphs when using the AT_LEAST line spacing rule. When I try to set a fixed line height with the AT_LEAST rule, it's always being set to EXACTLY instead.

For example, when I do something like this:

```python
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt
from docx.enum.text import WD_LINE_SPACING

document = Document()
paragraph = document.add_paragraph("This is a test paragraph with line spacing issues.")
paragraph_format = paragraph.paragraph_format

# Try to set line spacing with AT_LEAST rule
paragraph_format.line_spacing = Pt(14)
paragraph_format.line_spacing_rule = WD_LINE_SPACING.AT_LEAST

# But when I check the value:
print(paragraph_format.line_spacing_rule)  # Shows EXACTLY instead of AT_LEAST
```

The line spacing rule is being changed to EXACTLY regardless of what I set it to when using a Length object for the line_spacing value.

This is problematic because AT_LEAST and EXACTLY have different behaviors in Word - AT_LEAST allows text to expand beyond the specified height if needed (for larger fonts, etc.), while EXACTLY will clip text that exceeds the height.

Has anyone else encountered this issue? Is there a workaround?
</issue>
